viewer.stage:
WHILE YOU WERE OUT

20d
Warby Parker has sat at proposal for three weeks with no next step.
14d
Liquid Death has gone quiet — their people team is three deep and mid-launch.
8d
The Notion pilot is eight days in and two of four recruiters have not touched it.

And one you did not ask for — every deal you have won rode a dated expansion event. None of the cold ones landed.

viewer.cap: A live call. Discovery Studio is a console you run the call from, not notes you write after it. It shows the question, what to listen for, and the moment they answer you tap what you heard — it hands you the exact next line.
viewer.stage:
PAIN & CONSEQUENCE · MAKE THE COST REAL

Walk me through what happens the week a new store opens.

Listen for whether this pain is really theirs to fix, or a polite nice-to-have — and who flinches when you name the cost.

“It is messy but we cope”
“We just hired two more recruiters”
“Not a top priority”

They hired around it. Ask what that cost, and who signed it off — you have just found your economic buyer.

viewer.cap: A deal going quiet. Future Autopsy writes the story of how a deal dies before it does — names the pattern, counts the days you have left, and routes you to the room where the fix happens.
viewer.stage:
WRITTEN 45 DAYS EARLY

Warby Parker dies in 20 days, and here is how.

You have one champion and no one above him. Marcus goes quiet in week two, nobody signs, and it closes as no decision — the way most of your losses have gone.

Pattern
pressure before clarity
seen 4×
The smallest fix
get a second name in the room this week

20 minutes next week

THEY WILL PROBABLY SAY

“We are too small for something like this.”

Small teams feel a bad hire hardest. Ask what one wrong store manager cost them last year — nobody argues with a number they said out loud.

Read before you dial · log what happened after · never during

Say something useful on her post

Poppy accepted last week. Give her something today — do not ask yet.

LinkedIn. One account, one move. Watch what they post, say something useful about it, connect once they know your name, give something before you ask. The inbox is never the opening.
